name: Office Sample 5, section 5 Loss Estimates
source: Office Sample 5 - PRE 2026 - REDACTED.pdf, Section 4 (pp. 10-13; this template numbers it 5)

observations.note: 46 storeys + 3 bsmts. RC cols/beams, RC slabs, flat conc roof. internal walls masonry, core RC.
facade - unitised alu curtain wall, dbl glazed low-E / toughened. alu spandrels w 50mm rockwool. slab edge gap filled 135mm rockwool, 2hr. no combustible insulation on facade
office partitions drywall - gypsum, alu studs, rockwool infill
link to next bldg at B2 carpark, 2hr fire shutter. link not used, shutter perm shut

so the office floors are open plan, no separation within a floor except the utility rooms. elec rooms are 2 hour walls and floors with 2 hour doors, and every elec room we went into had the cable penetrations sealed
telecom risers triple vol, fire stopped every 3 flrs - the ones we saw ok. riser doors 1hr
internal stairs L27-29, L34-35, L40-41, L45-46. smoke det activated 2hr roller shutters round each stair
carpark all 3 bsmts, 351 lots + 6 accessible
tenant server room L5, approx 40 racks. UPS room next door, VRLA batteries. diesel genset at roof, 2 x 2000 kVA, day tank 1000 L, tested monthly on load per FM
3 x water cooled chillers B3, cooling towers on roof. 22 kV incomer from SP, 2 x transformers B1. no boilers. no hazardous storage apart from genset diesel
wet pipe sprinklers throughout incl car park, OH1 office / OH2 carpark. sprinkler tanks B3 2 x 300 m3. jockey + duty elec + standby diesel pump
few sprinkler heads recessed >50% into ceiling at B3 service corridor - obstructs spray pattern. FM said ceiling was lowered last yr
FM-200 in server room, last discharge/room integrity test 2023 - over due. no VESDA, only point smoke detectors
addressable fire alarm, monitored 24/7 by FCC on L1, direct link to SCDF. hose reels + extinguishers every floor, wet riser
weekly pump churn test logs ok but last annual flow test record not available. diesel pump fuel tank 3/4 full
bounded by public roads N and E, MRT station S (underground link closed off), 30 storey office W approx 25 m away
low lying area, PUB flood map - in flood prone zone. flood barriers at carpark ramp, manual, deployed by security on heavy rain warning. no flood since 2010 per FM
security 24/7, 6 guards per shift. CCTV ~300 cams recorded 30 days, monitored at FCC. card access turnstiles at lobby, lift destination control
loading bay manned 7am-10pm, after hours shutter locked + intruder alarm. carpark barrier + LPR
multi-tenant office, ~4000 occupants. building ERP exists, reviewed 2025, fire drill twice a yr. no BCP for the building itself - left to tenants. server room tenant has own DR site
CBD location, flat site approx 8,000 m2. SCDF fire stn ~2 km, response under 10 min per FM. hydrants on Rd N and E
construction site to the S across the road - 2 tower cranes, hot works on going. approx 40 m from our facade
lightning protection on roof, last tested 2025. windstorm - SG no typhoons, but sumatra squalls; roof plant tied down, curtain wall designed for wind load per FM
earthquake - SG low seismic zone, only tremors felt from sumatra quakes. no damage history. no seismic bracing on sprinkler pipes
B3 plant room + transformers in B1 below flood level. sump pumps x2 in B3, on genset supply, but no high water alarm to FCC

reference:
Level II Scenario
The PML scenario will be a fire starting within a tenant space on Level 27 with internal staircase leading upto L29 of [PROPERTY]. The fire may be caused by one of the following: fault in electrical fixture/appliance, improperly managed hot work activity, smoking, etc. As the building's sprinkler and automatic fire detection systems are assumed to be impaired (per the PML definition) the fire will reach a fully grown state and spread across the L27 floor plate due to an absence of horizontal fire compartmentation, and via continuity of combustibles. The fire will also spread vertically to 2 upper floors via internal unenclosed staircases from L27 to L29 (fire shutters won't be operational as fire detection systems are assumed to be impaired), prior to response by the emergency response team/fire brigade. The fire is expected to be contained at L29 with the timely response of emergency responders. Smoke, fire and water damage is anticipated to be sustained on L30 to L31, in addition to water damage in varying degrees to 5 floors below L27 (L22 to L26).

Level II Assumptions
Each floor from L27 to L29 is assumed to be 100% damaged (from fire/smoke), L30 to L31 is assumed to be 30% damaged (from smoke/water), while each floor from L22 to L26 is assumed to be 15% damaged (from water). Total number of floors in [PROPERTY] = 46 + 3. It will take about 1 month for investigation and clean-up, up to 7 months for full reinstatement works involving the fire-damaged floors (L27 to L31) to be completed. Tenants will not be able to operate out of the building/affected floors during the clean-up/reinstatement/recovery period and will have to relocate to other sites. For L22 to L26, tenants are still able to operate out of the existing units with ongoing repair for water damages. Assuming lost rental income for an 8 month period, the BI PML is estimated based on a percentage of affected lettable area.

Level III Scenario
The MFL scenario will be a fire starting within a tenant space on Level 27 (with internal staircase upto L29) of [PROPERTY]. The fire may be caused by one of the following: fault in electrical fixture/appliance, improperly managed hot work activity, smoking, etc. As the building's sprinkler and automatic fire detection systems are assumed to be impaired the fire will reach a fully grown state and spread across the L27 floor plate due to an absence of horizontal fire compartmentation, and via continuity of combustibles. With the local fire brigade assumed to be delayed for 2 hours (as per MFL), the fire will spread vertically to the upper floors via internal unenclosed staircases, breached floor penetrations and the building's exterior glass curtain walls, resulting in fire and associated smoke damage to 10 upper floors (i.e. L27 to L36). Water damage from a manual fighting (after 2 hours) will result in water damages in varying degrees to 10 floors below L27 (L26 to L17). The fire is not anticipated to spread to other Towers due to spatial separation and lack of continuous combustibles.

Level III Assumptions
Each floor from L27 to L36 is assumed to be 100% damaged (from fire/smoke), while each floor from L26 to L17 is assumed to be 15% damaged (from water). It will take about 2 months for investigation and clean-up, up to 14 months for full reinstatement works involving the fire-damaged floors (L27 to L36) to be completed, in addition to another 2 months for recovery of business to previous levels. Tenants will not be able to operate out of the building/affected floors during the clean-up/reinstatement/recovery period and will have to relocate to other sites. For L26 to L17, tenants are still able to operate out of the existing units with ongoing repair for water damages. Assuming lost rental income for an 18 month period, the BI PML is estimated based on a percentage of affected lettable area.
